'iskeyword' is `iskeyword=@,48-57,_,192-255` in both vim and nvim from a man.vim buffer, so not related to that.

    undefined variable: fname

this just looks like a netrw bug. Can you check the netrw version in both cases?
@justinmk how can I check the version of netrw?
Can't read the error message in your gif. That's the next step.

This is the error message

```
Error detected while processing function netrw#BrowseX:
line    4:
E121: Undefined variable: fname
E15: Invalid expression: (a:remote == 0 && isdirectory(a:fname)) || (a:remote == 1 && fname =~ '/$' && fname !~ '^https\=:')
:!elinks 'https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/issues' -source > '/var/folders/v1/4hv3mbqd7yv0sypr3gbst7j80000gn/T/nviml1nLN6/1'
```

Have the same netrw version in upstream vim, don't know why it does not occur in Vim, the problem seems to exists there as well.

I have been looking into it, it seems this patch should fix it:
```patch
diff --git a/runtime/autoload/netrw.vim b/runtime/autoload/netrw.vim
index 76485c2f3..ef19511e5 100644
--- a/runtime/autoload/netrw.vim
+++ b/runtime/autoload/netrw.vim
@@ -4970,7 +4970,7 @@ fun! netrw#BrowseX(fname,remote)
 "  call Dfunc("netrw#BrowseX(fname<".a:fname."> remote=".a:remote.")")

   " if its really just a directory, then do a "gf" instead
-  if (a:remote == 0 && isdirectory(a:fname)) || (a:remote == 1 && fname =~ '/$' && fname !~ '^https\=:')
+  if (a:remote == 0 && isdirectory(a:fname)) || (a:remote == 1 && a:fname =~ '/$' && a:fname !~ '^https\=:')
    norm! gf
 "   call Dret("netrw#BrowseX : did gf instead")
   endif
```

CC @cecamp
